w5-q1: Correct — interoperability enables different IoT devices and systems to communicate and exchange data.
Incorrect — interoperability is about devices working together, not restricting them to offline operation.
Incorrect — interoperability allows devices using different protocols to work together, so it is not limited to one protocol.
Incorrect — interoperability helps devices cooperate and does not disable other devices.
w5-q2: Correct — syntactic interoperability concerns the format of messages exchanged between devices and users.
Incorrect — battery size is a physical hardware property unrelated to message exchange.
Incorrect — device colour is a physical attribute and has nothing to do with interoperability.
Incorrect — sensor weight is a physical attribute and has nothing to do with message formats.
w5-q3: Correct — UMB stands for Universal Middleware Bridge, which helps different middleware-based devices work together.
Incorrect — Unified Mobile Board is not what UMB stands for.
Incorrect — Universal Memory Block is not what UMB stands for.
Incorrect — User Management Bridge is not what UMB stands for.
w5-q4: Incorrect — 3.3 V is the level used by some other boards and 3.3 V pins, but not the Arduino UNO operating voltage.
Correct — the Arduino UNO operates at 5 volts.
Incorrect — 9 V is a common battery voltage, not the UNO operating voltage.
Incorrect — 12 V is at the upper end of the recommended input supply range, not the UNO operating voltage.
w5-q5: Incorrect — a packet is a unit of data sent over a network, not a program written in the Arduino IDE.
Correct — a program created and uploaded using the Arduino IDE is called a sketch.
Incorrect — a frame is a link-layer data unit in networking, not an Arduino program.
Incorrect — a query is a request for information, not the name of an Arduino program.
w5-q6: Incorrect — HDMI is a video output interface and is not used to program an Arduino UNO.
Correct — the Arduino UNO connects to a computer through USB, used to upload programs and supply power.
Incorrect — VGA is a video display interface, not used to connect an Arduino UNO to a computer.
Incorrect — the standard UNO has no built-in Ethernet port; it needs a separate shield, and it is not the main computer link.
w5-q7: Incorrect — negative indices are not valid array positions in Arduino C/C++.
Correct — Arduino arrays are zero-based, as in C and C++, so the first element is at index 0.
Incorrect — index 1 is the second element, because indexing starts at 0.
Incorrect — index 2 is the third element, not the starting one.
w5-q8: Correct — the random() function generates a pseudo-random number within a specified range.
Incorrect — pinMode() configures a pin as input or output and does not generate random numbers.
Incorrect — digitalWrite() sets a digital pin HIGH or LOW and does not generate random numbers.
Incorrect — attachInterrupt() attaches an interrupt service routine to a pin and does not generate random numbers.
w5-q9: Incorrect — red represents stop and comes last in the sequence, not first.
Incorrect — yellow is the intermediate signal, switched on after green.
Correct — the traffic() function first sets the green LED HIGH to show the GO message, then switches to yellow and red.
Incorrect — the example switches the LEDs on in sequence, not all three together.
w5-q10: Correct — a DHT sensor measures the temperature and humidity of its surroundings.
Incorrect — distance and speed are measured by other sensors, such as ultrasonic sensors, not a DHT.
Incorrect — light and sound need different sensors, such as an LDR and a microphone, not a DHT.
Incorrect — pressure and altitude are measured by barometric sensors, not a DHT.
w5-q11: Incorrect — a sensor is an electronic element producing a signal, not a software program.
Incorrect — converting to mechanical motion is the job of an actuator, not a sensor.
Incorrect — a network address identifies a device on a network and is not what a sensor produces.
Correct — a sensor converts a physical quantity or measurement into an electrical signal.
w5-q12: Incorrect — delay() takes milliseconds, so 0.2 seconds would be delay(200).
Incorrect — 1 second would need delay(1000), not delay(2000).
Correct — delay() takes milliseconds, so delay(2000) equals 2000 ms, or 2 seconds.
w5-q13: Incorrect — the statement is false; a servo motor is high-precision and provides controlled rotary motion, not only linear motion.
Correct — a servo motor is a high-precision motor providing controlled rotary motion, so the statement is false.
w5-q14: Incorrect — an ultrasonic sensor measures distance and is a sensor, not a motion-producing actuator.
Incorrect — a DHT sensor measures temperature and humidity and does not produce motion.
Incorrect — a PIR sensor detects motion by sensing changes in infrared radiation; it is a sensor and does not produce rotary motion.
Correct — a servo motor is an actuator that provides precise and controlled rotary motion.
w5-q15: Correct — a stepper motor is one of the motor actuators discussed in the lecture.
Incorrect — the statement is true; a stepper motor is an actuator, so False is wrong.
